points.heading: Deepen: one-word times
points.body:
Today we stay on the **one-word** path only (no haber). Keep the thread: verb es action; conjugate es change for who/when; stem es fixed part; ending es tip. ## Key idea Let's explore together. Review the five clocks as one story: present, imperfect, preterite, future, conditional. The helpful contrast is cantaba (leaves the event open) versus canté (closes it). ## More examples One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**. Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**. Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words). Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.» Practice: Now it's your turn.

Práctica: Ahora te toca a ti.

Error común:

lesson.summary: This lesson teaches practice one-word times. Understand the central idea first, then explore it, practice it, and check a common mistake.
lesson.memoryPhrase: One word: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**. Two words: helper **haber** + already-done form (**he cantado**).
lesson.weekRecap: One word: canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría. Two words: helper haber + already-done form (he cantado). Learn to narrate WHEN an action happens: one-word forms and two-word forms (haber + already-done form), choosing with meaning.

questions.prompt: Which Spanish form shows an action happening now?
Which form tells about a finished action yesterday?

choices: A repeated or ongoing past action.
questions.answer: A repeated or ongoing past action.

questions.prompt: What two parts make a compound tense?
choices: A form of haber and a participle.
questions.answer: A form of haber and a participle.

questions.prompt: In «he cantado», which word is the participle?
Why should «comido» stay the same in «hemos comido»?
choices: It is always a future word.
The participle does not become plural for the subject.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct answer. **Canto** is mostly:
Which simple form can describe what someone would do?
Elige la respuesta que coincide con la actividad de hoy. Which one-word form means a possible action?
Piensa en la práctica de hoy. Which simple form can describe what someone would do?
¿Qué opción demuestra que entendiste la lección? Which one-word form means a possible action?
Busca el detalle importante. Which simple form can describe what someone would do?
Busca en el punto 1 («Deepen: one-word times») y escribe entre comillas las palabras exactas donde la clase habla de esto: Yesterday I **finished**. Luego explica con tus palabras qué entendiste.
Copia entre comillas la frase exacta del punto 1 («Deepen: one-word times») que mejor resume la idea principal. Después explica por qué esa frase es importante.

En el punto 1 («Deepen: one-word times»), encuentra y copia entre comillas las palabras exactas relacionadas con: I **was reading** when the phone **rang**. Explica qué significa esa idea en la clase de hoy.
Escribe entre comillas una cita exacta del punto 1 («Deepen: one-word times») que puedas usar para enseñarle a un compañero esta idea. Luego explica la cita con tus propias palabras.
